ideas.title: Symbolic-regression law for last fall degree d_F(n,l,m,t) with held-out extrapolation
ideas.statement: Fit closed-form candidates for d_F over the measured binary-descent and PKM-tower grid (n=13..45, l, m=3,4, t=1..14) by exhaustive search over a small grammar (floor/log/linear in l, n/l, t) with MDL penalty; hold out the largest n per (l,m). A law with d_F bounded in n at fixed l decides lever 1 empirically.
ideas.mechanism: Model-selection over presentation features (l, n mod small, ord_n(2), subspace type) rather than a single registered formula 4+floor((t-2)/4); distinguishes bounded vs log-growing d_F.
ideas.wall_bypassed: 'First fall degree is a constant of the presentation' leaves open whether d_F grows unboundedly; this targets exactly that open cell.
ideas.why_wall_hypotheses_fail: Closure fixes d_ff=2 and d_F<=k+2 but does not determine growth in n; a fitted bounded law with out-of-sample success is outside its scope.
ideas.nongenericity_argument: Accounting/theory only: if d_F = O(1) in n at l~n/m, Weil-descent oracle cost is poly(n)*2^{O(l)} and B*D^2 could drop below N; if d_F grows ~ l, no change. The regression itself does not change any exponent.
ideas.prior_art: Petit-Quisquater / Huang-Kosters-Yeo first-fall-degree heuristics; Kosters-Yeo 2015 counterexample data; Caminata-Gorla solving degree; programme falldegree.tex; 2304.13485; 2026/408 smoothed d_reg.

falsifier.design: Load existing d_F table (csd/fpn_degrees.py + treatise falldegree data); regenerate missing cells n=13..25 l=3..5 S_3 via msolve degree logging; fit grammar on n<=29, predict n=31..45 certified cells.
falsifier.toy_params: binary S_3 descent, n in {13,...,45 odd prime}, l in {3,4,5}, 30 random subspaces per cell
falsifier.prediction_if_true: A bounded law (max residual 0 on held-out, d_F plateau <=6 for l=4 across n) beats every growing law by MDL >= 5 bits
falsifier.prediction_if_false: Best held-out law grows in n or l with residual >=1 at >=2 held-out cells; registered 4+floor((t-2)/4) mispredicts at t>=10

ideas.risk: Measured grid too small/noisy; certified lower bounds (>=5) are censored data and must be handled as such.

ideas.title: Cheap pre-solve decomposability predictor with counted-operation accounting
ideas.statement: Train a classifier on features computable in O(n^2) bit ops from target x(R) and the subspace V (e.g. rank of the degree-1/2 linear part of the descended system after Frobenius folding, trace-form invariants, partial XL degree-2 rank deficit) to predict whether the descended S_3/S_4 system has a solution; skip trials predicted UNSAT. Gain counted in Gröbner operations saved per relation, leakage-controlled via csd train/test split on disjoint subspaces.
ideas.mechanism: Early-abort uses the field representation (degree-2 Macaulay rank deficit) as a certificate-like feature; distinct from E-ML-6 (exact-rule miner on residue/character vocab) and E-ML-2 (zero-row skipping inside one solve).
ideas.wall_bypassed: Generic oracle bound: features are representation-dependent (Weil-descent coordinates), so not GGM-simulable.
ideas.why_wall_hypotheses_fail: Generic bound covers membership tests by group ops; degree-2 rank deficit of descended equations is a field-representation statistic. Monodromy closure fixes mean yield but leaves variance/coverage free, which is what the predictor exploits.
ideas.nongenericity_argument: Constant-factor unless the predictor achieves recall ~1 at rejection fraction 1-2^{-c l}; then per-relation solve cost drops by the UNSAT fraction (~1-1/m!) at most, i.e. constant m!. Honestly engineering; an advance only if a polynomial feature decides decomposability (would be a new low-degree membership certificate, contradicting nothing proven over F_{2^n}).
ideas.prior_art: Trace-reuse / tracer F4 (2603.16378); Galbraith-Gebregiyorgis early abort; ML SAT satisfiability prediction (NeuroSAT); csd hardness predictor M7.

falsifier.design: Generate 4000 descended S_3 instances (n=17,l=6 so ~1/2 SAT); label by msolve; features from degree-2 Macaulay rank (python F_2 linear algebra); logistic regression + gradient boosting, train on 60 subspaces, test on 20 disjoint subspaces; count saved msolve matrix-ops at recall>=0.99.
falsifier.prediction_if_true: AUC>=0.75 on held-out subspaces; >=30% of UNSAT trials rejected at recall 0.99, net counted-op saving >=20% including feature cost
falsifier.prediction_if_false: AUC<=0.55 (indistinguishable from permutation null), no saving

ideas.risk: Degree-2 rank deficit may be identically constant (d_ff=2 everywhere), giving no signal.

ideas.title: Learned/annealed subspace (factor-base) selection minimising measured d_F, not yield
ideas.statement: Search over F_2-subspaces V of dimension l (parametrised by a basis in GL(n,F_2)/stabiliser) with simulated annealing + surrogate model whose objective is the measured solving degree and Macaulay matrix size of the descended S_3 system, beyond the gated log-linear yield model; test whether non-random subspaces exist with d_F strictly below the random-subspace distribution at fixed n,l.
ideas.mechanism: Optimises the presentation (the open d_F cell) directly; prior lever-6 bases were hand-picked families (trace-spectrum, Hamming-ball, mu_263), never optimised.
ideas.wall_bypassed: No-subfield closure leaves non-invariant subspaces open with cost = solving degree; monodromy closure leaves solving difficulty free.
ideas.why_wall_hypotheses_fail: No Frobenius-stable subspace exists at prime n, but the closure says nothing about d_F distribution across non-invariant subspaces.
ideas.nongenericity_argument: If a learned family has d_F = c independent of n, oracle cost becomes poly and B*D^2 << N follows via standard Diem-style accounting; if gains are <=1 degree at toy n with no family structure, it is constant-factor.
ideas.prior_art: Diem 2011 (subexp over F_{q^n}); Petit-Kosters-Messeng; Huang-Kosters-Petit-Yeo-Yun quasi-subfield polynomials (closed); Learning Fast Monomial Orders (2602.02972) analogous search over orders.

falsifier.design: n=19, l=5: sample 300 random subspaces, record msolve max degree and matrix size on 5 targets each; then 300 annealing steps (bit-flip in basis) minimising mean degree; recompute on 20 fresh targets for top-5 found subspaces.
falsifier.toy_params: n=19, l=5, S_3, 5 targets/eval, annealing budget 300
falsifier.prediction_if_true: Optimised subspaces show mean max-degree >=1 below random median on fresh targets, with matrix size reduction >=4x
falsifier.prediction_if_false: Optimised degree within the random distribution's 5-95% band on fresh targets (overfit to training targets)

ideas.risk: Degree distribution over subspaces may be essentially constant; cost evaluation per subspace may be too slow for 300 steps.

ideas.title: Rank-aware relation collection via learned column-coverage policy (GNN-free baseline first)
ideas.statement: In relation collection, choose next target/trial subspace to maximise expected rank increase of the sparse relation matrix over Z/r, using a policy learned on the relation hypergraph (column degree, unhit columns); compare relations needed to reach full rank vs the k-XORSAT/random baseline factor.
ideas.mechanism: Targets the excess-relation factor and coverage variance (free per monodromy closure), not mean yield.
ideas.wall_bypassed: Monodromy closure (mean yield double count) — leaves variance/coverage free.
ideas.why_wall_hypotheses_fail: Closure fixes expected yield per trial, not which columns get hit; directed selection can reduce the coupon-collector excess.
ideas.nongenericity_argument: Constant-factor only: at best removes the log B coupon-collector factor in relations; cannot move B*D^2 relative to N. Classified engineering/accounting.
ideas.prior_art: Coja-Oghlan et al. k-XORSAT threshold (2301.09287); structured Gaussian elimination / filtering in NFS; Joux-Vitse relation counts.

falsifier.design: Toy prime-field E/F_p p~2^20, B=500 x-interval base, m=2 decompositions by table; random-target collection vs greedy policy that picks target multiples whose candidate relations hit low-degree columns (decided only after decomposition - honest cost); count trials to full rank mod r.
falsifier.toy_params: p~2^20, r prime, B=500, 50 runs each policy
falsifier.prediction_if_true: Policy needs >=15% fewer trials to full rank, counting all trials
falsifier.prediction_if_false: Trials within 3% of random (policy cannot steer since targets are random by construction)

ideas.risk: Targets [a]P+[b]Q are uniform; steering impossible without non-generic preview, likely null.

ideas.title: Learned variable order / XOR-branching for WDSat on descended systems, priced in propagations
ideas.statement: Train a one-shot ranking (features: variable's occurrence in Frobenius-folded XOR clauses, degree in S_3 descent) for WDSat/cryptominisat branching on descended S_3/S_4; measure growth exponent of conflicts+propagations in l at n=17..25 vs default; test whether the exponent (not constant) changes.
ideas.mechanism: Exploits the subspace-coordinate structure (l free vars, rest determined) to branch only on l basis coefficients with Gaussian XOR propagation — learned order generalised across n; distinct from E-ML-4 by requiring exponent-in-l measurement and transfer.
ideas.wall_bypassed: Generic oracle bound (representation-dependent SAT on Weil-descent coordinates).
ideas.why_wall_hypotheses_fail: SAT on descended equations uses bit-level field structure.
ideas.nongenericity_argument: Branching on l variables costs >=2^{l/c}; any advance needs c>1 effective, i.e. learned order prunes exponentially. Likely constant-factor; classified engineering unless fitted exponent of conflicts vs l drops below the default by >=0.2 per variable.

falsifier.design: Encode descended S_3 (CNF-XOR) for n=17,19,21,23, l=4..8, 40 SAT targets per cell; default cryptominisat5 vs order from features trained at n=17,19; fit log2(propagations) vs l.
falsifier.prediction_if_true: Slope of log2 propagations in l reduced by >=0.2 at n=23 (transfer)
falsifier.prediction_if_false: Slope unchanged within 0.05; any gain a constant offset

ideas.risk: Default XOR Gauss-Jordan already near-optimal; gains collapse at transfer.
